title: Construction Jobs — General Contractor and Project Manager
body: Public edition. Public employment reference, fact-checked. The general contractor runs the whole job: bidding, scheduling trades, ordering materials, managing the budget, and answering to the owner and inspectors. Typical path: years as a carpenter or other trade, then lead carpenter, then superintendent, then contractor. Licensing varies by state — most require a contractor's license exam plus proof of experience and insurance. Pay range (US, 2024-2026): roughly 70,000 to 130,000 dollars per year for residential GCs, higher for commercial. Key skills: reading plans, scheduling, cost control, contracts, and people management. Employment: self-employed, or employed by construction firms. Outlook: steady — every building needs someone to run the job.

title: Construction Jobs — Carpenter
body: Public edition. Public employment reference, fact-checked. Carpenters build the wood skeleton: framing, formwork, trim, stairs, and cabinets. Path: apprenticeship (typically 3-4 years) through a union or open-shop program, or learning on the job under a lead carpenter. Pay range (US, 2024-2026): roughly 40,000 to 75,000 dollars per year, with union scale higher in major cities. Skills: plan reading, layout math, power-tool mastery, and an eye for plumb, level, and square. Employment: residential framers, finish carpenters, union commercial carpenters, or self-employed. Outlook: strong — framing and remodeling demand stays high.

title: Construction Jobs — Electrician
body: Public edition. Public employment reference, fact-checked. Electricians install and maintain power, lighting, and control systems. Path: 4-5 year apprenticeship with classroom hours, then the journeyman exam; master electrician after more years and a second exam. Pay range (US, 2024-2026): roughly 55,000 to 100,000+ dollars per year. Skills: code knowledge (NEC), conduit bending, troubleshooting with meters, and strict safety discipline — electricity does not forgive mistakes. Employment: residential, commercial, industrial, or maintenance electricians; many go independent. Outlook: excellent — electrification and data centers keep demand high.

title: Construction Jobs — Plumber
body: Public edition. Public employment reference, fact-checked. Plumbers install water, drain, waste, vent, and gas systems and keep them working. Path: 4-5 year apprenticeship, then journeyman license; master plumber later. Pay range (US, 2024-2026): roughly 50,000 to 95,000+ dollars per year, with emergency and commercial service at the top. Skills: code knowledge, soldering and press-fitting, reading isometric drawings, and diagnostic troubleshooting. Employment: residential service, new construction, commercial, or self-employed. Outlook: excellent — pipes always need people.

title: Construction Jobs — Mason and Bricklayer
body: Public edition. Public employment reference, fact-checked. Masons build with brick, block, and stone — walls, chimneys, fireplaces, and pavers. Path: 3-4 year apprenticeship, learning mortar mixing, coursing, and trowel work on the job. Pay range (US, 2024-2026): roughly 45,000 to 80,000 dollars per year. Skills: mortar consistency, level coursing, cutting and fitting units, and reading masonry details. Employment: residential masonry contractors, commercial masonry firms, restoration specialists. Outlook: steady — masonry is slow to automate.

title: Construction Jobs — Heavy Equipment Operator
body: Public edition. Public employment reference, fact-checked. Heavy equipment operators run excavators, dozers, loaders, graders, and cranes. Path: training school or union apprenticeship, then seat time; crane operators need NCCCO certification in the US. Pay range (US, 2024-2026): roughly 50,000 to 90,000+ dollars per year, crane operators higher. Skills: machine control finesse, grade reading, soil awareness, and radio communication with ground crews. Employment: earthwork contractors, road builders, quarries, crane companies. Outlook: good — infrastructure spending drives demand.

title: Construction Jobs — Construction Laborer
body: Public edition. Public employment reference, fact-checked. Laborers are the hands of the job: carrying material, cleaning up, digging, assisting trades, and running small tools. Path: no formal apprenticeship required — start as a helper and learn; OSHA 10 safety training is the standard entry credential. Pay range (US, 2024-2026): roughly 35,000 to 55,000 dollars per year. Skills: reliability, physical stamina, basic tool use, and safety awareness. Employment: every contractor hires laborers; union laborer programs exist in many cities. Outlook: steady — the best laborers become apprentices in a trade.

title: Construction Jobs — Building Inspector
body: Public edition. Public employment reference, fact-checked. Building inspectors verify that permitted work meets code: foundations, framing, electrical, plumbing, and finals. Path: years in a trade or construction, then inspector certification (ICC exams are the US standard) and employment by a city or county. Pay range (US, 2024-2026): roughly 55,000 to 85,000 dollars per year. Skills: deep code knowledge, diplomacy (failing work without starting fights), thorough documentation, and plan-reading. Employment: municipal building departments, third-party inspection firms. Outlook: steady — retirements keep openings coming.
